articles.title: The chocolate bar that melted next to a radar: the story of the birth of the microwave
articles.standfirst: He accidentally discovered that microwaves could heat food while working during World War II
articles.summary: He accidentally discovered that microwaves could heat food while working during World War II
articles.body:
D uring World War II, radar became a decisive technology for detecting enemy aircraft and submarines. Behind those systems was a fundamental component: the magnetron , a device capable of generating microwaves. In one of the laboratories of the American company Raytheon, Percy Spencer worked there, a self-taught engineer who would end up finding an unexpected application for that technology.

In 1945, while conducting tests near an operating magnetron, Spencer noticed that the chocolate bar he had in his pocket had melted.

From popcorn to the first oven

His next experiment was with corn kernels. He placed them near the device and watched as they began to pop into popcorn . He then tried an egg, which ended up exploding due to the pressure building up inside it. Those tests gave him a clue: the energy emitted by the magnetron could also be used for cooking.

Spencer then devised a metal box in which to concentrate the microwaves and heat food in a controlled way. Raytheon saw the potential of the idea and filed a patent application for a microwave cooking process in October 1945 . The patent was granted in 1950.

The first commercial model, christened Radarange, reached the market in 1947 . However, it was very far from today’s household appliances : it stood around 1.8 meters tall, weighed hundreds of kilos, and had a high price. Its size and cost initially limited its use to restaurants, industrial kitchens, and other professional spaces.

The technology needed decades of improvements to reach homes. The models became smaller and more affordable, eventually turning that accidental discovery into a common household appliance . Spencer, who amassed more than a hundred patents during his career, did not start out with a project to revolutionize kitchens: he simply noticed a melted chocolate bar and wanted to find out why it had happened.

articles.title: Pitbull and his private life: “I’m very reserved about what I do, so I don’t want to bring them into my world; it’s my responsibility as a father to protect them”
articles.standfirst: The singer is very protective of his private life
articles.summary: The singer is very protective of his private life
articles.body:
What we are used to is celebrities exposing their private lives, whether of their own free will or simply because of the exposure that comes with their profession itself. However, there are celebrities who resist the public exposure of their privacy and those around them. One of those people is Pitbull, who keeps his private life in the utmost confidentiality , choosing to keep his parental duties completely out of the media spotlight. In fact, as he told Billabong: “I’m very reserved about what I do, so I don’t want to bring them into my world; it is my responsibility as a father to protect them."

The importance of maintaining privacy

Having a private life should not be a luxury, but a necessity. It is not only good, but necessary for our well-being. It is important to understand that it can give us peace of mind and less anxiety by not forcing yourself to expose every detail on social media or to third parties. It is very stressful to have to seek extreme validation or compare yourself to others. It is a way of not owing anyone any explanations nor having to expose our loved ones or have them question your decisions as a father, husband, or person.

Being famous or well-known is not the only way to feel exposed; you can also feel that exposure on social media or in real life. But setting that exposure aside allows you to have greater focus and greater authenticity that help you build projects or go through processes in silence, allowing you to make mistakes, reflect, and grow without the pressure of feeling that you cannot fail.

Furthermore, not exposing those we love and our privacy allows us to protect your reputation and relationships as well as those of your loved ones and to have a personal safety network that limits the amount of vulnerable information.

But if there is one type of overexposure that is even more harmful, it is that of children, since it can even become dangerous for them. One of the duties we have is to ask for consent , encouraging dialogue and consulting at least before sharing any content involving minors, also helping to foster dialogue on this issue and reflection on whether it is the best course of action or not.

In addition, we must be cautious and avoid sensitive data about the minor, without showing clearly identifiable faces, nudity, school information and, of course, we should never post in real time. If you want to share something, it is advisable to keep the circles closed and strictly limit the audience to very close family members, and periodically review the privacy settings of the accounts and social networks we use.

articles.title: The curious English remedy from the High Middle Ages that scientists have reconstructed for its effectiveness against bacteria
articles.standfirst: A mixture that is now being put to the test
articles.summary: A mixture that is now being put to the test
articles.body:
Centuries ago, human beings did not have the medical and technological advances of today and, therefore, diagnosing and treating certain illnesses was an almost impossible task. In the search for a product that could relieve a patient, all around the world remedies were created that, in a way, helped those affected, and based on this a cure was developed.

In the High Middle Ages , an English remedy became very popular due to its supposed effectiveness against bacteria . Now, the scientific community has come together to recreate that mixture and thus be able to verify firsthand whether, in fact, it lives up to that medical premise or not and can be used in the future.

The main objective of this medieval remedy against bacteria

It is the Bald's eye ointment . An English physician was the original author of this recipe, which mixed wine, garlic, onion, and ox bile . Its aim was to combat styes and, according to today’s experts, its laboratory results were surprising: it was able to damage the membranes of dangerous bacteria, such as Staphylococcus aureus .

Over two weeks, the bacteria became more resistant to antibiotics than to the medieval remedy , so this ointment could now be used as a basis for the development of future mixtures that can be employed in the antibacterial fight and that represent an alternative to already known remedies.

One alarming figure is that, for example in 2021, antibiotic resistance could be associated with more than 4.5 million deaths worldwide . Remedies like this one from the High Middle Ages could serve as an example so that the medical community has more tools within reach and patients have more and better options when it comes to combating certain ailments.

articles.title: The four terrifying and enigmatic predictions of Nostradamus for 2027
articles.standfirst: The famous prophecies of the French apothecary are once again at the center of international controversy after the dark scenarios that would mark the year 2027 were revealed
articles.summary: The famous prophecies of the French apothecary are once again at the center of international controversy after the dark scenarios that would mark the year 2027 were revealed
articles.body:
The prophecies of Michel de Nostredame , universally known as Nostradamus , continue to generate an unshakable fascination as new calendar cycles approach. Written in the 16th century in a poetic format known as quatrains and grouped into centuries, their enigmatic lines have been reinterpreted from generation to generation. Historians and scholars of the occult recall that the French physician and astrologer published his masterwork in 1555, achieving enormous notoriety after the death of King Henry II of France, an event that many interpreted as his first great accurate clairvoyant prediction .

Over the centuries, occultism enthusiasts have tried to fit the seer’s verses to events of major global significance, from the Great Fire of London to the most critical moments of the 20th and 21st centuries. However, the academic community insists on maintaining a stance of rigorous skepticism toward these readings . Specialists point out that the original texts lack explicit dates and that their literary ambiguity allows them to be freely shaped so that they retrospectively match almost any historical catastrophe or contemporary crisis .

The specific linking of these predictions to the year 2027 stems from a modern method of analysis popularized by the mystic’s followers. Traditionally, many interpreters use quatrain number 27 from the different centuries to associate it directly with the current year, an interpretive device foreign to the author’s original intent. Despite the lack of scientific rigor, the arrival of this period has once again raised alarm among prophecy enthusiasts , who closely analyze the verses in search of warnings about humanity’s immediate future .

Cursed treasures and ancient mysteries

One of the most disturbing passages recovered by experts in ancient cryptography describes an oak tree struck by lightning and the revelation of a treasure hidden for centuries. The legend accompanying these verses includes a chilling warning for any daring soul who tries to unearth the riches: the prophecy states that the discoverer will suffer a violent death with a sharp object piercing their eye . This dramatic description has fueled all kinds of theories for decades about ancestral curses protecting forgotten fortunes in remote corners of the planet.

Modern researchers of Nostradamus's writings often directly associate this passage with the intense explorations carried out on Oak Island , an enigmatic island located off the coast of Canada. For generations, treasure hunters have invested millions in excavating the land in search of a supposed hidden loot, a quest that has gained enormous worldwide notoriety thanks to television productions such as the documentary program The Curse of Oak Island. Although excavation teams have recovered various metallic artifacts and historical remains, the great treasure still has not appeared .

Despite the lack of tangible evidence, followers of the prophecies insist that 2027 could be the key year in which this age-old mystery is finally resolved in a tragic way . For their part, local historians and folklore experts remind us that the supposed curse is part of the popular mythology built around the North American island and not a proven supernatural warning. The fascination with the enigmas of the underground shows how ancient texts continue to fuel the appetite for the unknown.

Armed conflicts and tensions in the Black Sea

The international geopolitical chessboard also does not escape the darkest interpretations of the quatrains for the coming cycle. Various prophecy analysts highlight verses that explicitly speak of fire, deployments of heavy weaponry, and an alleged military advance from Persian territory toward the ancient region of Trebizond . In current cartography, this geographic point corresponds to the modern Turkish city of Trabzon, strategically located in the vicinity of the turbulent waters of the Black Sea, an area historically sensitive to global security.

In contemporary geopolitical readings, the mention of Persia is usually interpreted as a direct allusion to the Islamic Republic of Iran and its role in Middle Eastern tensions. International security analysts, such as expert Jiang Xueqin, have repeatedly warned about the risks of a large-scale military escalation and massive civil unrest that could destabilize the global economy . Nostradamus's quatrains describe scenarios in which the waters of the seas are stained with blood, imagery that alarmists use to predict armed confrontations with continental repercussions.

Faced with these catastrophic readings, international relations experts urge caution and remind us that using sixteenth-century texts to anticipate modern military conflicts lacks empirical validity. Nevertheless, some interpreters suggest that Turkey could play a crucial role as a mediator in potential peace negotiations , mitigating the crisis before it reaches irreversible proportions. The ambiguity of the verses leaves multiple hypotheses open about the future of global diplomacy and stability in Eurasia.

The financial collapse and the fall of great wealth

The economic sphere is another of the fundamental pillars in the interpretations circulating about the year 2027. The verses analyzed by specialists in alternative finance describe symbolic images of gold and silver with artificially inflated values that end up being thrown into the fire and consumed by the flames. These passages suggest a scenario of widespread bewilderment in which the great accumulated fortunes lose their market value overnight, unleashing a profound crisis of confidence in international markets and shaking the foundations of the global capitalist system .

Economists and macroeconomics experts point out that this interpretation finds a curious parallel with current warnings about the uncontrolled growth of sovereign public debt among the world's major powers. From this analytical perspective, the precious metals mentioned in the quatrains would function as a perfect metaphor for the fictitious wealth and financial speculation that characterize modern markets. Financial analysts warn that the fragility of the current monetary system exposes the global economy to drastic and unforeseen corrections .

Despite the concern generated among small investors, economists emphasize that Nostradamus never predicted a specific financial crisis for 2027 and that any current correlation is the product of retrospective reinterpretation . Warnings about inflation and the collapse of overvalued assets are part of the usual economic cycles of contemporary capitalism. However, the appeal of finding in Renaissance poetry a warning about today’s financial fragility keeps the most pessimistic observers of the global economy on alert.

articles.title: In 1978, two children found a Ferrari buried in their home's garden: behind it was an alleged insurance fraud
articles.standfirst: The Ferrari Dino 246 GTS had disappeared in 1974 and was found in 1978 beneath the garden of a house in Los Angeles
articles.summary: The Ferrari Dino 246 GTS had disappeared in 1974 and was found in 1978 beneath the garden of a house in Los Angeles
articles.body:
There are discoveries that seem straight out of a movie, but happen by chance. In February 1978, two children playing in the garden of their home in Los Angeles (United States) started digging in the ground and found something they did not expect: a Ferrari Dino 246 GTS that had been buried for four years. What began as a game ended up uncovering a story of disappearance, an insurance payout, and an alleged fraud that was never completed as planned.

The children were digging when their shovels struck something strange beneath the grass. After removing some of the earth, they found some plastic and a green metal surface . The family alerted the authorities, and several officers went to the house to investigate the discovery. At first, the scene was so baffling that investigators even considered whether there might be something else underground.

The excavation revealed that what had been buried was a 1974 Ferrari Dino 246 GTS , a highly valuable Italian sports car. The vehicle had been protected with plastic sheeting, blankets, and other materials in an attempt to prevent moisture and dirt from damaging it during the time it remained hidden.

A disappeared Ferrari and an insurance payout

The license plate and the chassis number made it possible to quickly identify the car. It belonged to Rosendo Cruz, a plumber from California who had bought it new in 1974 for $22,500 . Just a few weeks after purchasing it, he reported that it had been stolen.

Since the car did not turn up, the insurance company ended up paying him compensation for its disappearance. However, the 1978 discovery completely changed the course of the case.

Years later, an informant provided investigators with a version according to which the Ferrari's disappearance had allegedly been part of an insurance fraud scheme . According to that account, the owner had allegedly hired several people to make the vehicle disappear so he could collect the insurance payout . The plan was to get rid of the sports car, but those who were given the job allegedly decided not to destroy it.

Instead of sinking it in the Pacific Ocean or dismantling it to sell its parts, they chose to bury it whole on a plot of land that was undeveloped at the time. The intention was supposedly to recover it once the matter had been forgotten. However, the place eventually became a residential area, and houses were built on the land. The car ended up beneath one of them, and no one ever came back for it.

The Ferrari was restored after its discovery

The passage of years underground left significant damage to the vehicle. Moisture had affected the bodywork and the interior, while the extraction also caused damage. Despite this, the Ferrari aroused enormous interest because of its history, and the insurance company decided to put it up for sale.

The car passed through the hands of several owners until it was acquired by an enthusiast who drove its restoration . The specialist in charge of the work managed to bring the engine back to life and recover much of its original appearance.

The sports car's story became forever linked to its unusual discovery. Its owner even decided to personalize the license plate with the inscription " DUG UP ", which in English means " dug up ". A direct reference to the four years the Ferrari spent hidden underground before two children, who were simply playing in their home's garden, brought it to light.

articles.title: Søren Kierkegaard, Danish philosopher: "Life is not a problem to be solved, but a reality to be experienced"
articles.standfirst: The famous reflection encourages people to stop treating existence as a series of challenges to overcome and instead appreciate the experiences that make life meaningful
articles.summary: The famous reflection encourages people to stop treating existence as a series of challenges to overcome and instead appreciate the experiences that make life meaningful
articles.body:
Life can often feel like an endless sequence of problems waiting to be fixed. People spend years making plans, pursuing ambitions and worrying about what comes next, sometimes forgetting to appreciate what is happening around them.

A widely circulated philosophical quotation offers a different perspective: "Life is not a problem to be solved, but a reality to be experienced."

The words are frequently associated with Søren Kierkegaard , the Danish philosopher whose work explored human existence, personal responsibility, faith and the difficulties of making meaningful choices.

Although the quotation captures ideas that are closely associated with his philosophy, there is an important detail behind its popularity: there is no reliable evidence that Kierkegaard actually wrote or said these exact words.

The wording appears to be a variation of a sentence published by Dutch writer and philosopher Jacobus Johannes van der Leeuw in his 1928 book The Conquest of Illusion. His original formulation was: "The mystery of life is not a problem to be solved; it is a reality to be experienced."

The distinction matters because the phrase has circulated under Kierkegaard's name for decades, appearing on quotation websites and in collections of inspirational sayings.

Nevertheless, its underlying message provides an interesting starting point for understanding the Danish philosopher's approach to existence.

Born in Copenhagen on May 5, 1813, Kierkegaard became one of the most influential thinkers of the 19th century. His writings challenged people to examine their beliefs, decisions and relationships with the world rather than simply accepting the expectations of society.

Why Kierkegaard believed individual experience mattered

Kierkegaard is frequently described as a founding figure of existentialism, a philosophical tradition concerned with individual existence, freedom and the responsibility people have for their choices.

One of his central concerns was the difference between understanding something intellectually and actually living through it. He questioned the idea that human existence could be explained entirely through abstract theories or universal systems.

For Kierkegaard , becoming an individual involved making personal decisions and accepting the uncertainty that accompanied them. People could not simply rely on other people's expectations to determine how they should live.

This perspective helps explain why the popular quotation feels consistent with his broader philosophy, even if its attribution is questionable.

His personal life also influenced his writing. Kierkegaard spent much of his life in Copenhagen and became particularly interested in questions surrounding faith, anxiety, love and the individual's relationship with God.

His relationship with Regine Olsen was especially significant. The couple became engaged in 1840, but Kierkegaard subsequently broke off the engagement. The experience continued to influence his reflections on commitment, sacrifice and personal responsibility.

Among his most important publications were Either/Or (1843), Fear and Trembling (1843) and The Concept of Anxiety (1844). These works examined different aspects of human decision-making and the emotional consequences of living with uncertainty.

The real author behind the famous quotation

The history of the quotation adds another dimension to its meaning. Van der Leeuw 's The Conquest of Illusion, published in 1928, contains the earlier version of the sentence, predating many of the later appearances that credited Kierkegaard .

Reference collections including Wikiquote have highlighted the disputed attribution, while the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy provides a detailed account of Kierkegaard's actual philosophical contributions.

Ultimately, the quotation remains popular because its message is easy to recognise. Life cannot always be organised into neat objectives, and not every difficult experience has an immediate solution.

Its appeal lies in encouraging people to appreciate relationships, unexpected opportunities and ordinary moments instead of becoming consumed by what they have yet to achieve.

Kierkegaard died in Copenhagen on November 11, 1855, aged 42, but his influence on philosophy, theology and literature continues.

Whether readers encounter the famous sentence under his name or Van der Leeuw 's, its central idea remains relevant: existence is not simply something to manage or control. It is something to participate in, understand and experience.

A widely circulated philosophical quotation offers a different perspective: "Life is not a problem to be solved, but a reality to be experienced."

The words are frequently associated with Søren Kierkegaard , the Danish philosopher whose work explored human existence, personal responsibility, faith and the difficulties of making meaningful choices.

Although the quotation captures ideas that are closely associated with his philosophy, there is an important detail behind its popularity: there is no reliable evidence that Kierkegaard actually wrote or said these exact words.

The wording appears to be a variation of a sentence published by Dutch writer and philosopher Jacobus Johannes van der Leeuw in his 1928 book The Conquest of Illusion. His original formulation was: "The mystery of life is not a problem to be solved; it is a reality to be experienced."
The distinction matters because the phrase has circulated under Kierkegaard's name for decades, appearing on quotation websites and in collections of inspirational sayings.
Nevertheless, its underlying message provides an interesting starting point for understanding the Danish philosopher's approach to existence.

Born in Copenhagen on May 5, 1813, Kierkegaard became one of the most influential thinkers of the 19th century. His writings challenged people to examine their beliefs, decisions and relationships with the world rather than simply accepting the expectations of society.
Why Kierkegaard believed individual experience mattered

Kierkegaard is frequently described as a founding figure of existentialism, a philosophical tradition concerned with individual existence, freedom and the responsibility people have for their choices.

One of his central concerns was the difference between understanding something intellectually and actually living through it. He questioned the idea that human existence could be explained entirely through abstract theories or universal systems.

For Kierkegaard , becoming an individual involved making personal decisions and accepting the uncertainty that accompanied them. People could not simply rely on other people's expectations to determine how they should live.
This perspective helps explain why the popular quotation feels consistent with his broader philosophy, even if its attribution is questionable.

His personal life also influenced his writing. Kierkegaard spent much of his life in Copenhagen and became particularly interested in questions surrounding faith, anxiety, love and the individual's relationship with God.

His relationship with Regine Olsen was especially significant. The couple became engaged in 1840, but Kierkegaard subsequently broke off the engagement. The experience continued to influence his reflections on commitment, sacrifice and personal responsibility.

Among his most important publications were Either/Or (1843), Fear and Trembling (1843) and The Concept of Anxiety (1844). These works examined different aspects of human decision-making and the emotional consequences of living with uncertainty.
The real author behind the famous quotation

The history of the quotation adds another dimension to its meaning. Van der Leeuw 's The Conquest of Illusion, published in 1928, contains the earlier version of the sentence, predating many of the later appearances that credited Kierkegaard .

Reference collections including Wikiquote have highlighted the disputed attribution, while the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy provides a detailed account of Kierkegaard's actual philosophical contributions.
Ultimately, the quotation remains popular because its message is easy to recognise. Life cannot always be organised into neat objectives, and not every difficult experience has an immediate solution.
Its appeal lies in encouraging people to appreciate relationships, unexpected opportunities and ordinary moments instead of becoming consumed by what they have yet to achieve.
Kierkegaard died in Copenhagen on November 11, 1855, aged 42, but his influence on philosophy, theology and literature continues.

Whether readers encounter the famous sentence under his name or Van der Leeuw 's, its central idea remains relevant: existence is not simply something to manage or control. It is something to participate in, understand and experience.

articles.title: On Neptune, it rains diamonds, and some scientists have managed to make them on Earth using plastic bottles
articles.standfirst: The method could replace explosives in the industrial production of nanodiamonds
articles.summary: The method could replace explosives in the industrial production of nanodiamonds
articles.body:
Turning the plastic from a water bottle into diamonds sounds like science fiction, but it is already a reality in the laboratory. A team of physicists from the Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR) and the University of Rostock , in Germany , has managed to produce ten trillion nanodiamonds with each laser shot at a thin sheet of PET, the material used for bottles.

The big breakthrough is not only creating them, but having managed to recover them intact for the first time. The results are published in the journal Diamond and Related Materials .

The process is simple in appearance. A high-power laser hits the plastic three times per minute and generates a shock wave that compresses it to about 100 gigapascals, nearly a million times atmospheric pressure. In just a few nanoseconds, the carbon rearranges itself and forms diamonds.

The challenge came afterward: the crystals are shot out at more than ten kilometers per second, like a meteorite, and any rigid surface would destroy them. The solution was to place a soft gel behind the plastic that slows the impact and, when dissolved in water, releases the particles intact.

Each diamond measures about three nanometers and contains around 3,000 carbon atoms. “It was a special moment after years of work” , summarizes Ben Heuser, the study’s first author.

From Neptune's diamond rain to quantum sensors

The research originated to simulate the interior of Uranus and Neptune , where it is believed that diamonds rain down from methane subjected to enormous pressures. Now, the method could offer an alternative to current industrial production, which uses explosives and produces crystals with metal residues that have to be cleaned with acid.

Nanodiamonds are already used for polishing and, since the new method makes it possible to dope them with other atoms, they could be adapted for quantum sensors or contrast agents in magnetic resonance imaging. That said, three shots per minute are still not enough for industry, and the team is already thinking about a laser capable of firing ten times per second.

articles.title: In Alaska, an entire town lives in the same 14-story building, which houses the post office and the police station: people go to school through a tunnel, and the road closes at night
articles.standfirst: One of the most spectacular places on the planet
articles.summary: One of the most spectacular places on the planet
articles.body:
There are remote cities and towns that most people know nothing about and would be unable to locate and, above all, they would be surprised if they knew the living conditions. In Alaska , for example, there is an entire town whose inhabitants live in the same 14-story building , which also houses the post office, the Town Hall, the grocery store, and the police station.

It is located on the shores of an Alaskan fjord, and the town is called Whittier , at the beginning of the Passage Canal . It is surrounded by the state's steep mountains and has just over 250 inhabitants .

One building houses 85% of the population

What is curious about this place lies precisely in the way those people live, and everything revolves around the Begich Towers, a 14-story building with 196 apartments . It is a kind of hotel at the foot of the glaciers where, according to local data, around 85% of the population lives . The other 15% is located in another building, although a smaller one.

Another striking fact is that Whittier has no streets with single-family homes or garden areas; instead, the entire town is the apartment block itself. It was built in the 1950s by the United States Army so that military personnel and their families could stay there, since it had been a strategic point during World War II .

Once the army left the area in the early 1960s, the city bought the building and in 1974 it was renamed Begich Towers, in honor of Nick Begich, an Alaska congressman who died in 1972 in a plane crash. Inside are all the amenities for the residents: city hall, the police station, the supermarket, the laundromat, the medical clinic, and the church occupy the lower floors.
